impact.description: 1st place at the MSOE AI Club Hacksgiving hackathon

case_study.context: The Milwaukee Domes Alliance wanted to increase visitor engagement and revenue. The project was completed during a 50-hour MSOE AI Club hackathon.
case_study.my_role: UX product designer and researcher; presenter.
case_study.action: Interviewed the CEO and education director, researched visitor needs, prototyped AI visitor experiences in Figma, field-tested the concept, and presented it.
case_study.result: The tested concept combined a plant-focused voice assistant, AI-generated tours, and a photo-based scavenger hunt. The team won first place.
case_study.summary: Designed and tested an AI-powered experience to grow visitor engagement and revenue for the Milwaukee Domes Alliance.

impact.description: less configuration time through my workflow redesigns

case_study.context:
L & S Electric needed a modern desktop app for configuring and controlling its 
                AES-110 and AES-1100 hydro-electric power excitation systems. The users are electrical engineers
                    and field technicians (both inside and outside of L & S Electric, Inc.) working live with power generation equipment, where a misread
                    value or mis-click has drastic consequences. The app had to combine real-time metering, a
                    multi-channel oscilloscope, COMTRADE fault-file analysis, synchroscope and capability
                    curve displays, and automated control sequences.
case_study.my_role: Lead User Experience Designer, Researcher, and Writer
case_study.action:
Stakeholder research: I ran working sessions with L & S electrical engineers to
                    understand how they commission, tune, and troubleshoot excitation systems, and
                    which readings they need side by side during each task. I also shadowed a technician
                    through a commissioning workflow on the legacy tool.
                    Information architecture: I organized screens into task-based modes
                    (configuration, monitoring, control, fault analysis) so engineers could move between
                    them without losing context. A/B testing with 4 to 5 engineers shaped the
                    navigation.
                    Interaction design for high-stakes control: I designed the auto-control and sequence
                    screens with clear state indicators, confirmation steps for irreversible commands, and
                    consistent placement of critical readings while making sure to follow L & S's own accessibility and HMI standards.
                    Data visualization: I designed the oscilloscope and COMTRADE views — channel
                    toggles, zoom bands, and RMS/frequency/phase measurement readouts — so
                    engineers could isolate a fault window quickly.
                    Design system: I created a reusable component library (gauges, metering tiles, alarm
                    states) that let development scale consistently.
                    Validation: I reviewed builds with engineers each iteration and refined layouts based
                    on what they actually looked for first, conducting usability walkthroughs at roughly every
                    two to four weeks. I also experimented with field testing during QA testing for AES-110s.
case_study.result:
One unified, scalable tool replaced several outdated tools for configuring, monitoring,
                    and analyzing excitation systems. 
                    Configuration time decreased by about 50%. 
                    Engineers can analyze historical fault events in the same oscilloscope interface they
                    use live, shortening root-cause analysis from hours to minutes.
                    Consistent patterns across all pages reduce training time for new technicians
                    and lower the risk of operator error on live equipment.
                    The product gives L & S a modern, branded software experience to pair with their
                    hardware in customer sales.

impact.description: 2nd place in the MSOE AI Club Discovery World hackathon

case_study.context: Discovery World needed a cost-effective, technology-based way to make exhibits more accessible. The project ran for 50 hours.
case_study.my_role: UX researcher and designer; presentation creator.
case_study.action: Observed visitors using existing accessibility tools, consulted stakeholders, identified user needs, and prototyped a Bluetooth-locator chatbot with age-adjusted exhibit responses.
case_study.result: The team earned second place with a low-cost accessibility concept designed to require little effort from visitors.
case_study.summary: Designed an accessible, age-aware exhibit chatbot for Discovery World with the MSOE AI Club.

impact.description: High-fidelity sustainable soap-bottle prototype; no quantified impact reported

case_study.context: The 14-week industrial design project aimed to create a sustainable physical product ready for theoretical publication.
case_study.action: Researched comparable products, refined CAD and mold designs, 3D-printed molds, tested materials, and iterated from feedback.
case_study.result: Created a high-fidelity prototype of a hand-soap bottle made from recycled hotel soaps, with a reusable soap outer bottle.
case_study.summary: Designed a reusable hand-soap bottle made entirely from soap to reduce packaging waste.
